title: A base converter
description:
Read lines with `read_line`. Each holds one unsigned number written in decimal (`255`), hexadecimal (`0xff` or `0XFF`) or binary (`0b11111111`). Parse it **yourself** and print it in all three bases:

```
255 = 0xff = 0b11111111
```

For the input

```
255
0x1F
0b101
0
banana
0x
12z
```

print

```
255 = 0xff = 0b11111111
31 = 0x1f = 0b11111
5 = 0x5 = 0b101
0 = 0x0 = 0b0
not a number: banana
not a number: 0x
not a number: 12z
```

The numbers fit in 64 bits. Write your own printing too: you may use `print_str` and `print_char` for text, but not `read_int`, `print_int`, `print_uint`, `print_hex` or `print_bin`. One function that prints in any base (dividing by the base, with a table of digit characters) does all three.

starter.main.asm:
global  _start
        section .bss
line:   resb    100

        section .text
_start:
.next:
        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        mov     esi, 100
        call    read_line
        cmp     rax, -1
        je      .exit
        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        call    print_str
        call    print_newline
        jmp     .next
.exit:
        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

solution.main.asm:
global  _start
        section .bss
line:   resb    100
out:    resb    72

        section .data
digits: db      "0123456789abcdef"
s_eq_hex: db    " = 0x", 0
s_eq_bin: db    " = 0b", 0
s_bad:  db      "not a number: ", 0

        section .text
; parse_digits: rdi = text, rsi = base. Returns the value in rax, and rdx = 1 if the text was
; one or more valid digits and nothing else, otherwise 0.
parse_digits:
        xor     eax, eax
        xor     r8d, r8d                ; digits seen
.next:  movzx   ecx, byte [rdi]
        test    cl, cl
        jz      .end
        lea     edx, [rcx - '0']
        cmp     edx, 9
        jbe     .have
        or      ecx, 0x20
        lea     edx, [rcx - 'a']
        cmp     edx, 5
        ja      .bad
        add     edx, 10
.have:  cmp     rdx, rsi
        jae     .bad
        imul    rax, rsi
        add     rax, rdx
        inc     r8
        inc     rdi
        jmp     .next
.end:   xor     edx, edx
        test    r8, r8
        setnz   dl
        ret
.bad:   xor     edx, edx
        ret

; print_base: rdi = an unsigned number, rsi = base. Prints it.
print_base:
        lea     r8, [rel out + 71]
        lea     r9, [rel digits]
        mov     rax, rdi
.digit: xor     edx, edx
        div     rsi
        movzx   ecx, byte [r9 + rdx]
        mov     [r8], cl
        dec     r8
        test    rax, rax
        jnz     .digit
        inc     r8
        lea     rdx, [rel out + 72]
        sub     rdx, r8
        mov     rsi, r8
        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        syscall
        ret

_start:
.next:
        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        mov     esi, 100
        call    read_line
        cmp     rax, -1
        je      .exit

        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        mov     esi, 10
        cmp     byte [rdi], '0'
        jne     .parse
        movzx   eax, byte [rdi + 1]
        or      eax, 0x20
        cmp     eax, 'x'
        jne     .maybe_bin
        mov     esi, 16
        add     rdi, 2
        jmp     .parse
.maybe_bin:
        cmp     eax, 'b'
        jne     .parse
        mov     esi, 2
        add     rdi, 2
.parse:
        call    parse_digits
        test    rdx, rdx
        jz      .bad
        mov     rbx, rax

        mov     rdi, rbx
        mov     esi, 10
        call    print_base
        lea     rdi, [rel s_eq_hex]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, rbx
        mov     esi, 16
        call    print_base
        lea     rdi, [rel s_eq_bin]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, rbx
        mov     esi, 2
        call    print_base
        call    print_newline
        jmp     .next
.bad:
        lea     rdi, [rel s_bad]
        call    print_str
        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        call    print_str
        call    print_newline
        jmp     .next
.exit:
        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: Look at the first two characters to choose the base: `0x`/`0X` is 16, `0b`/`0B` is 2, otherwise 10. Then the same loop works for all: `value = value * base + digit`, refusing any digit that is not valid in that base.
Print the result with `print_uint`, `print_hex` and your own binary printer (or `print_bin` with the number of significant bits).
rules: Parse and print the numbers yourself.
